media_work.title: David & Me
media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, juvenile conviction, friendship between filmmaker and inmate, advocacy leading to exoneration.
media_work.summaryNotes: Highlights the role of personal connection and persistent advocacy in overturning a conviction.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, juvenile conviction, friendship between filmmaker and inmate, advocacy leading to exoneration.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Chronicles filmmaker Ray Klonsky's efforts to help free David McCallum, wrongfully convicted of murder at age 16. Directed by Ray Klonsky & Marc Lamy. Available via Amazon Prime, DVD, Festivals.
research_notes_other.research_findings: This documentary follows the personal journey of Ray Klonsky, who began corresponding with David McCallum as a teenager. Their friendship evolved into an effort, documented by Klonsky and co-director Marc Lamy, to investigate McCallum's decades-old conviction, highlighting coerced confessions and weak evidence. The film captures the long fight involving lawyers and advocates like Rubin Carter, culminating in McCallum's exoneration in 2014.

contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confession (obtained at age 16), inconsistent evidence, advocacy highlighting case flaws.
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated (Conviction vacated by Brooklyn DA's Conviction Review Unit)
organizations_involved_raw: Filmmakers Ray Klonsky & Marc Lamy; Pro-bono legal team; Rubin "Hurricane" Carter (advocate).
featured_individuals.**also_implicated: ** Willie Stuckey (Co-defendant, convicted alongside McCallum, died in prison 2001, conviction also vacated posthumously 2014)
